product.name: Amp

names: Amp CLI on a remote machine

notFor: phone path is mobile web, not a native app
Megawatt high/ultra not included by default

sections.heading: Identity and current status
sections.body:
- Project ID: `amp`
- Canonical name: Amp (`claim-amp-sf-identity`)
- Vendor: Amp Frontier Corporation (`claim-amp-sf-vendor`)
- Canonical URL: https://ampcode.com/ (`claim-amp-sf-canonical-url`)
- Current status: actively shipped commercial product (`claim-amp-sf-status`)
- Last source-backed identity check: 2026-08-15
- Public source repository for Amp itself: unknown (`claim-amp-sf-repository-url`)
- Current CLI version: unknown (`claim-amp-sf-version`)

sections.heading: What it is and is not
sections.body:
- What it is: a frontier coding agent that runs locally, on the web, on a phone, and in orbs (`claim-amp-sf-what-it-is`)
- What it is not: not a self-hosted deployment (`claim-amp-sf-what-it-is-not-self-hosted`). The documented phone path is mobile web, not a native app (`claim-amp-sf-what-it-is-not-native-mobile`). JetBrains is deprecated (`claim-amp-sf-surface-jetbrains-deprecated`)

sections.heading: Architecture and agent-loop ownership
sections.body:
- Primary type: `runtime` (`claim-amp-sf-primary-type`)
- Secondary role: `cloud-agent` for orbs (`claim-amp-sf-secondary-role-cloud`)
- Agent-loop owner: Amp Server authorizes inference and stores threads; Amp Client executes tools (`claim-amp-sf-agent-loop-owner`)
- Architecture: remote-controllable, compaction-first, plugin-powered CLI (`claim-amp-sf-architecture`); later copy calls Amp a distributed system with durable agent-loop execution (`claim-amp-sf-architecture-durable`)

sections.heading: Surfaces and execution location
sections.body:
- Surface IDs: `surface-amp-cli`, `surface-amp-web`, `surface-amp-web-remote-client`, `surface-amp-runner`, `surface-amp-mobile-web`, `surface-amp-slack`, `surface-amp-vscode`, `surface-amp-zed`, `surface-amp-neovim`, `surface-amp-sdk`, `surface-amp-cli-remote-shell`
- Execution location: same-device for default CLI (`claim-amp-sf-execution-local`); vendor-cloud Debian 12 orb per web-started thread (`claim-amp-sf-execution-orb`); user-controlled host for `amp --no-tui` runners (`claim-amp-sf-execution-runner`)

sections.heading: Model/auth/provider strategy
sections.body:
- Model strategy: four mode presets plus Puck; routes change with subscriptions and availability (`claim-amp-sf-model-strategy`). Dated 2026-08-15 catalog includes GPT-5.6, Claude Fable 5, GLM-5.2, and Gemini 3.7 Flash (`claim-amp-sf-model-catalog`). Manual high+ChatGPT Oracle routing (`claim-amp-sf-oracle-manual-chatgpt`) conflicts with the Modes ChatGPT-sub tab (`claim-amp-sf-oracle-modes-chatgpt`)
- Auth strategy: sign in at ampcode.com (`claim-amp-sf-auth-sign-in`); password, enterprise SSO via WorkOS, passkeys for remote control (`claim-amp-sf-auth-strategy`); `AMP_API_KEY` for headless CLI and SDK (`claim-amp-sf-auth-api-key`). ChatGPT and X Premium+/SuperGrok subscription reuse (`claim-amp-sf-subscription-reuse`). BYOK on unconstrained (`claim-amp-sf-byok`)
- Provider support: Amp-proxied US inference across the listed providers (`claim-amp-sf-provider-support`)

sections.heading: Context, memory, compaction, and session behavior
sections.body:
- Context behavior: client-assembled snippets, open-file metadata, and editor state (`claim-amp-sf-context-behavior`); AGENTS.md and @-mentions (`claim-amp-sf-context-agents-md`)
- Memory: AGENTS.md, personal/workspace skills, and searchable threads (`claim-amp-sf-memory`)
- Compaction: automatic at 90% window (`claim-amp-sf-compaction`); Compaction system model listed as GPT-5.6 Sol (`claim-amp-sf-compaction-model`)
- Session behavior: synced threads with queue, steer, archive, continue, and cross-thread references (`claim-amp-sf-session-behavior`)

sections.heading: Tools, extensions, MCP, skills, hooks, and APIs
sections.body:
- Tools: shell plus specialist tools; catalog via `amp tools list` (`claim-amp-sf-tools`)
- Extensions: Amp Plugin API (`claim-amp-sf-extensions`)
- MCP: client for local and remote servers; workspace servers need approval; orb OAuth MCP not yet supported (`claim-amp-sf-mcp`)
- Skills: Agent Skills with project, personal, workspace, and Claude-compatible paths (`claim-amp-sf-skills`). A May 2026 post said add/remove/update commands were removed (`claim-amp-sf-skills-neo-removed-commands`)
- Hooks: plugin lifecycle events (`claim-amp-sf-hooks`); orb `.agents/setup` and `.agents/resume` (`claim-amp-sf-hooks-orbs`)
- APIs: TypeScript/Python SDK (`claim-amp-sf-api`); stream-json CLI (`claim-amp-sf-api-stream-json`); orb plugin webhooks (`claim-amp-sf-api-orb-webhooks`); enterprise data-management API (`claim-amp-sf-api-data-management`)

sections.heading: Orchestration and parallelism
sections.body:
- Orchestration: subagents, Oracle, Librarian, Puck, and plugin-created orb threads (`claim-amp-sf-orchestration`)
- Parallelism: isolated parallel subagents (`claim-amp-sf-parallelism`); many concurrent orbs; numeric cap unknown (`claim-amp-sf-parallelism-orbs`)

sections.heading: Isolation, permissions, security, and data path
sections.body:
- Isolation: e2b ephemeral compute for Amp sandboxes (`claim-amp-sf-isolation`); per-thread orbs (`claim-amp-sf-isolation-orbs`); local CLI sandbox not established (`claim-amp-sf-isolation-local`)
- Permissions: default is no approval; optional permissions plugin (`claim-amp-sf-permissions`)
- Security: SOC 2 Type II, TLS 1.2+, AES-256, secret redaction, enterprise SSO (`claim-amp-sf-security`)
- Data path: US GCP thread store; partial code to providers; training opt-in except enterprise never (`claim-amp-sf-data-path`)

sections.heading: Interface inventory plus remote/mobile/background behavior
sections.body:
List each surface from `surfaces.jsonl` separately. Keep native mobile, first-party mobile web, first-party messaging, vendor relay, remote client, private-network, Termux/mobile terminal, and generic remote shell routes distinct.

- Interface and surface IDs:
  - CLI / TUI: `surface-amp-cli` (`claim-amp-sf-surface-cli`)
  - Web (orb start): `surface-amp-web` (`claim-amp-sf-surface-web`)
  - Web remote-client of CLI/runner: `surface-amp-web-remote-client` (`claim-amp-sf-surface-web-remote-control`)
  - Runner: `surface-amp-runner` (`claim-amp-sf-surface-runner`)
  - Desktop web via `amp app`: `claim-amp-sf-surface-amp-app` (not a `desktop-app` surface)
  - Mobile web: `surface-amp-mobile-web` (`claim-amp-sf-surface-mobile-web`)
  - Slack: `surface-amp-slack` (`claim-amp-sf-surface-slack`)
  - VS Code IDE connect: `surface-amp-vscode` (`claim-amp-sf-surface-ide`)
  - Zed IDE connect: `surface-amp-zed` (`claim-amp-sf-surface-ide`)
  - Neovim IDE connect: `surface-amp-neovim` (`claim-amp-sf-surface-ide`); keep beside `claim-amp-sf-nvim-deprecated`
  - Retired VS Code/Cursor editor extensions: first-party essay says they self-destruct 5 Mar 20:00 PT (`claim-amp-sf-extensions-self-destruct`). This is not CLI `ide connect`. Keep `claim-amp-sf-surface-ide`.
  - SDK: `surface-amp-sdk` (`claim-amp-sf-surface-sdk`)
  - Generic remote shell for CLI: `surface-amp-cli-remote-shell` (`claim-amp-sf-remote-ssh-bell`)
- Remote behavior: orb start/resume, web remote-control of CLI, and user-hosted runners (`claim-amp-sf-remote-access`). First-party vendor-relay, private-network, and Termux routes were not established as named product surfaces
- Mobile behavior: mobile web; native apps unknown (`claim-amp-sf-mobile-access`)
- Background behavior: unsupervised orbs auto-pause after five idle minutes (`claim-amp-sf-background`); keep working after the laptop is closed (`claim-amp-sf-background-laptop`); agents set schedules and wake with saved context (`claim-amp-sf-background-schedules`); start agents from Slack (`claim-amp-sf-background-slack`); plugin webhooks wake an orb (`claim-amp-sf-api-orb-webhooks`)

sections.heading: Pricing, license, maintenance, and lock-in
sections.body:
- Pricing: Megawatt $20, Gigawatt $200, usage billing (`claim-amp-sf-pricing`); orbs $0.08–$1.32/hour (`claim-amp-sf-pricing-orbs`)
- License: product open-source license unknown (`claim-amp-sf-license`); amp.nvim is Apache-2.0 (`claim-amp-sf-license-nvim`)
- Maintenance: actively maintained (`claim-amp-sf-maintenance`); users run `amp update` (`claim-amp-sf-maintenance-update`). amp.nvim is separately deprecated (`claim-amp-sf-nvim-deprecated`)
- Lock-in related facts: no self-hosted deployments (`claim-amp-sf-what-it-is-not-self-hosted`); Amp account required (`claim-amp-sf-auth-sign-in`); ChatGPT/Grok reuse and BYOK are documented (`claim-amp-sf-subscription-reuse`, `claim-amp-sf-byok`)

sections.heading: Lineage and compatibility edges
sections.body:
- Lineage claims: spin-out of Sourcegraph (`claim-amp-sf-lineage-sourcegraph`); Amp Neo rebuilt then renamed Amp (`claim-amp-sf-lineage-neo`); plugins inspired by Pi (`claim-amp-sf-lineage-pi-plugins`)
- Relationship edges: unknown. No directed tuple was added. Inspiration by Pi is not `fork_of` or `wraps_cli`. Claude Code compatibility is not a wrapper (`claim-amp-sf-compatibility-claude`)
- Compatibility: CLAUDE.md fallback and Claude skill paths unless disabled (`claim-amp-sf-compatibility-claude`). `--stream-json-thinking` is not Claude Code compatible (`claim-amp-sf-api-stream-json`)

sections.heading: Closest substitutes, partial substitutes, same-lineage relatives, often-confused products, and complements

- Same-lineage relatives: unknown

sections.heading: Unique edge, meaningful drawbacks, best fit, and not-for
sections.body:
- Unique edge: frontier modes plus unsupervised orbs across web, CLI, and phone (`claim-amp-sf-unique-value`); Slack @Amp on the orbs marketing page (`claim-amp-sf-unique-value-slack`)
- Meaningful drawbacks: default unsupervised tool execution (`claim-amp-sf-drawback-default-no-approval`); no OAuth MCP in orbs yet (`claim-amp-sf-drawback-orb-oauth-mcp`); no self-host (`claim-amp-sf-what-it-is-not-self-hosted`); Neovim plugin docs disagree (`claim-amp-sf-surface-ide`, `claim-amp-sf-nvim-deprecated`)
- Best fit: people who want the most out of an agent (`claim-amp-sf-intended-user`); teams and enterprises on unconstrained/enterprise pricing (`claim-amp-sf-intended-user-teams`)
- Not-for: self-hosted (`claim-amp-sf-what-it-is-not-self-hosted`); Megawatt high/ultra by default (`claim-amp-sf-not-for`); maintained JetBrains (`claim-amp-sf-surface-jetbrains-deprecated`)

claims.claim: Amp Chronicle still publishes first-party news and features an item dated 13 Aug 2026.
claims.notes: Scoped per review to the cited /chronicle page. The homepage news list is a separate page and is already canonical in claim-amp-sf-maintenance; it is not restated here.

claims.claim: The pricing page says students and teachers can subscribe to Amp Megawatt for 50% off with an honor-system education discount.
claims.notes: Honor declaration only. No verification process is specified on this page.

claims.claim: The August 11, 2026 news post says plugins and skills are now Amp-hosted, work everywhere Amp runs, and live in personal and workspace settings.
claims.value: Amp-hosted personal and workspace plugins and skills
claims.notes: Post also says workspace admins can push workspace plugins/skills that load by default.

claims.claim: The same post tells users to run amp skill update <name> or amp plugins update <name>, or ask Amp to update imported skills.
claims.notes: Keep beside the May 6, 2026 Neo claim that add/remove/update skill commands were removed.

claims.claim: Amp is the current Amp Frontier Corporation identity.
Security docs split Amp into Amp Client, which executes tools, and Amp Server at ampcode.com, which authenticates, stores threads, authorizes inference, and has thread actors call LLM providers.
claims.value: Amp Server owns inference and thread state; Amp Client executes tools
claims.notes: Distributed-system wording is claim-amp-sf-architecture-durable.

claims.claim: The Amp SDK lets TypeScript or Python programs drive the Amp agent, including streaming, multi-turn threads, MCP config, skills, and permissions. Docs say the TypeScript SDK uses the Amp CLI. Access is via AMP_API_KEY. execute() can continue the latest thread or continue by thread ID.
claims.value: TypeScript/Python SDK; CLI dependency; AMP_API_KEY; continue-by-id
claims.notes: stream-json is claim-amp-sf-api-stream-json. Orb webhooks are claim-amp-sf-api-orb-webhooks. Data-management API is claim-amp-sf-api-data-management.

claims.claim: The security reference says Amp exposes a data-management API for workspace analytics and thread data so enterprise security teams can connect scanning and response workflows.
The Orbs manual says an Amp plugin can create a public HTTP webhook endpoint that stores events and wakes its orb. Webhooks work only in plugins running in Amp-managed orbs.
The Owner's Manual documents --stream-json with --execute for one JSON object per line on stdout. --stream-json-thinking extends the schema and is not Claude Code compatible.
claims.value: CLI --stream-json; thinking flag not Claude Code compatible
claims.notes: The page does not say default stream-json tries to be Claude Code compatible. Do not infer that.

claims.claim: The May 6, 2026 rebuild post says the rebuilt Amp CLI runs on a new architecture that is remote-controllable, compaction-first, and plugin-powered.
claims.notes: Distributed-system / durable-execution wording is claim-amp-sf-architecture-durable.

claims.claim: The June 4, 2026 Agents Everywhere post says Amp is now a distributed system with durable execution for the agent loop and a plugin API.
claims.value: distributed system with durable agent-loop execution

claims.claim: The Owner's Manual non-interactive section says to set the access token in AMP_API_KEY.
claims.value: AMP_API_KEY access token for headless CLI and SDK
claims.notes: SDK page independently documents export AMP_API_KEY. This row cites the manual.

claims.claim: The Owner's Manual Get Started step 1 is to sign in at ampcode.com.

The security reference says Amp Enterprise supports Single Sign-On and Directory Sync through identity providers including Okta, provided by WorkOS. SSO can be exclusive, preventing password-based authentication. Password sign-in is documented; passkeys can be required for remote-controlling threads.
claims.value: ampcode.com account; password; enterprise SSO via WorkOS; passkeys for remote control
claims.notes: Email/Google buttons were on the /install sign-in wall and are not used as product proof. AMP_API_KEY is claim-amp-sf-auth-api-key.

claims.value: unsupervised orbs auto-pause after five idle minutes
claims.notes: Laptop-closed is claim-amp-sf-background-laptop. Schedules are claim-amp-sf-background-schedules. Slack start-from-Slack is claim-amp-sf-background-slack. Plugin webhooks that wake an orb are claim-amp-sf-api-orb-webhooks.

claims.notes: Compaction system model GPT-5.6 Sol is claim-amp-sf-compaction-model on /modes.

claims.claim: The Modes page checked 2026-08-15 lists Compaction as a system model for context summarization of long threads, using GPT-5.6 Sol.
If no AGENTS.md exists in a directory but CLAUDE.md does, Amp includes that file. Amp also loads Claude-compatible skill directories unless amp.skills.disableClaudeCodeSkills is set.

When a developer starts a new thread, the Amp Client collects local contextual information such as code snippets, metadata about open files, and relevant editor state, then sends the prompt, history, and tool results through Amp Server to the model.
claims.value: client-assembled snippets, open-file metadata, and editor state
claims.notes: AGENTS.md and @-mentions are claim-amp-sf-context-agents-md on the manual.

claims.claim: Primary infrastructure is GCP in the US. Amp stores threads and partial code context, not the entire codebase. Providers see selected context. Training is off unless opted in; enterprise workspaces can never enable training.

claims.notes: Linked ChatGPT or Grok consumer terms are separate from Amp's training toggle.

claims.claim: Default tool use has no approval prompt. Amp warns that untrusted repositories, MCP servers, and other inputs can influence what it does.
The MCP docs say orbs do not yet support OAuth-authenticated MCP servers.
claims.value: no OAuth MCP in orbs yet

claims.claim: The default CLI path runs Amp on the user's machine and executes tools against the local workspace.
Each orb thread started from ampcode.com gets a fresh Debian 12 remote machine with a cloned repository, plugins, and preinstalled tools.

claims.claim: A user-controlled machine running amp, including amp --no-tui, can act as a runner so ampcode.com can start threads in that directory.
